newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end spiritless trade slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end spiritless trade slightly higher.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended slightly higher on Thursday. Participants remained sidelined as even a slew of corporate earnings results failed to serve as an incentive, brokers said, adding that the government's package of financial deregulation measures would take time to implement.
The key Nikkei 225 average gained 51.60 points, or 0.25 percent, to close at 21,031.04. Its December futures were 30 points higher at 21,090.
"There is nothing to serve as fresh incentives from a fundamental point of view," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Turnover was a thin 248 million shares, down from 314 million shares on Wednesday.
Declining issues outpaced advancers 548 to 457, while 209 issues were unchanged.
The TOPIX index of all first section stocks was up 2.07 points or 0.13 percent to end at 1,569.85, and the Nikkei 300 average was also up 0.70 points or 0.24 percent to 294.84.

Brokers said Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's financial deregulation plan released earlier this week was welcomed by the market, but they would adopt a wait-and-see attitude until all the ministries involved implement his plan successfully.
"We cannot see an action programme yet," Higashida said.
A string of corporate earnings results, which will peak on Friday, has yet to provide clues to the strength of the economic recovery.
"The earnings results are showing nothing surprising," said Kenichi Sagami, general manager of the stock department at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
"It would not be too late to evaluate the results after most earnings come out," he said.
Brokers also said that reaction to currency movements has been muted recently.
Market participants are waiting for any remarks on currencies by influential Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, who will speak at a meeting in Tokyo from 0830 GMT.
Some brokers said trade may pick up after the outcome of the Bank of Japan's quarterly survey of business sentiment to be released later this month.
Among sectors, losers were led by precision instruments, communications, brokerages, construction and transportation equipment.
The major gaining sectors were pharmaceuticals, nonferrous metals, pulp/paper, services and oil.

Shares in Nippon Credit Bank continued to fall on Thursday, even after the bank denied a report on Wednesday that it had guaranteed a financially troubled non-bank unit's loans to agricultural financial institutions.

The share price dropped 23 yen to close at 306 yen, below its previous low for this year at 326 yen. It was ranked as the second largest percentage loser in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Shares of some companies were lifted by favourable earnings results.
Nippon Sanso Corp rose eight yen to end at 487 yen. Sanshin Electronics Co Ltd jumped 80 yen to 1,550 yen and Ricoh Co Ltd gained 20 yen to 1,170 yen.
Shares in Mitsumi Electric Co Ltd climbed on hopes of higher earnings for the company in the latter half of this business year, traders said.
Mitsumi Electric was up 50 yen to 2,090 yen.

Meanwhile, the second section index was down 3.06 points to 2,026.43, in turnover of 13.93 million shares. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was also down 0.29 points to 1,461.66. -- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
